Source-only PASS for authored distinctness. Frozen task prefix P=.qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-extension-scope2/task. P/instruction.md:1-9 asks for a local JavaScript/HTML/CSS playground with preview and console, recovery of the last working preview, and safe simultaneous saved-snippet editors. P/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5-21 gives product-specific execution semantics: fresh JS document, complete HTML/CSS modes, cancellation of pending callbacks, a shared five-second run budget, retained interactive successful previews, entered-source error locations, and structured console output. These are actual authored workflows, not only renamed entities: P/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:45-105 separately grades filename dispatch, CSS sample rendering, fresh globals, completed-preview interactions, supersession, Stop and rollback. P/task.toml:5-16 consistently identifies this as the programming/devtools product and declares its supplied Colderwater provenance.
Compared available sibling product metadata and the closest editor-like tasks. PatchPad's source brief/editing note and tests/functional/judge.toml:115,204 concern grapheme deletion, selection and exact find/replace; GridForge's spreadsheet note and tests/functional/judge.toml:104,139 concern formula precedence and range-plus-scalar recalculation; Boardloom tests/functional/judge.toml:80,100 concern attached connectors and grouped geometry. The shared save/revision/theme patterns do not make these the same flows. Colderwater fits the available suite portfolio as a code-execution tool. The frozen template instruction.md:1 is a CHANGE_ME stub and template functional judge has generic change_me/persistence criteria; preserving that shared harness is not evidence of a cloned product.
Adversarial source thought experiment: rename a PatchPad-style text editor's document to 'snippet', keep save/conflict controls, and add a static preview. It still lacks executed filename dispatch, callback supersession and rollback required by Colderwater's cited criteria; no authored-distinctness loophole was found. Conforming alternative considered: use a different editor component, different labels/routes and a pending-run overlay that retains the good render. P/environment/instructions/policy.md:5 and tests/app_context.md:12,18 permit those choices; resemblance in generic shell structure does not make that implementation a sibling clone. These are source inferences, not executed app trials.
